record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.original_question: For functions on the N-dimensional torus T^N, N≥2, the paper proves a stronger phase-control estimate in H^{1/2}+W^{1,1} and explains that the same method would follow from the unresolved inequality ||φ-∫φ||_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} ≤ C ||∇φ||_{H^{1/2}+L^1}. Does this estimate hold for every scalar function φ?

evidence.quote: If we try to establish (7.5) by the same method as above we would need to invoke a stronger version of (7.3); namely (7.6) ||φ − ∫φ||_{H1/2 + W1,1} ≤ C ||∇φ||_{H1/2 + L1}. However, such an estimate is still undecided. Open Problem 7.1 ([4]). Does (7.6) hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N \ge 2$ and let $\mathbb{T}^N = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^N$ denote the $N$-dimensional torus. For a scalar function $\varphi : \mathbb{T}^N \to \mathbb{R}$, denote by $\fint \varphi = \int_{\mathbb{T}^N} \varphi$ its mean value.

Recall the sum-space norms: for two Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ of distributions on $\mathbb{T}^N$, the space $X+Y$ is equipped with the norm
$$\|u\|_{X+Y} = \inf\{\|u_1\|_X + \|u_2\|_Y : u = u_1 + u_2,\ u_1 \in X,\ u_2 \in Y\}.$$
Here $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)$ is the Sobolev space of order $1/2$, $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)$ is the Sobolev space of $L^1$ functions whose distributional gradient is in $L^1$, and $\|\nabla \varphi\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}$ denotes the sum-space norm of the gradient considered componentwise (i.e.\ $\nabla \varphi = F + G$ with $F \in H^{1/2}$, $G \in L^1$, and one takes the infimum of $\|F\|_{H^{1/2}} + \|G\|_{L^1}$).

Does there exist a constant $C = C(N) > 0$ such that for every scalar function $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{T}^N$ one has
$$\Big\| \varphi - \fint \varphi \Big\|_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} \le C\, \|\nabla \varphi\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A recent 2025 preprint resolves "Open Problem 1.1" from Brezis's list of favorite open problems (the Brezis–Nirenberg problem on the 3-ball), but does not address this sum-space estimate. No source located indicates a resolution of the inequality in $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ controlled by $\|\nabla\varphi\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}$, which is recorded as undecided. It appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution
status_evidence.snippet: We provide a complete resolution to the first one—Open Problem 1.1—in Brezis's favorite open problems list.
status_evidence.claim: A 2025 paper resolves Open Problem 1.1 (Brezis–Nirenberg on the 3-ball), distinct from the sum-space gradient estimate at issue here.

status_evidence.title: Some of my favorite open problems (Brezis)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem list including endpoint Bourgain–Brezis-type estimates.
status_evidence.claim: The inequality concerning $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ versus $H^{1/2}+L^1$ is listed as an undecided open problem.
